transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Priya (Velox Head of ML), Liam (Velox Infra), Sofia (Velox SecOps), Daniel (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
- Kickoff for onboarding Velox onto Redwood Private/Dedicated evaluation. Discussed network, security controls (KMS, SSO), initial QoS/latency SLOs, pilot plan (7-14 day benchmark), and next steps for staging tests. Agreed to share network checklist, pricing, and run initial smoke tests.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm going to kick us off. quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the runbooks and network.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya here, i'm the head of ML at Velox. good to meet you all.
[00:15] Liam: Liam, infra.
[00:17] Sofia: Sofia, security.
[00:19] Daniel: Daniel product.
[00:21] Maya: Maya, solution engineering Redwood.
[00:23] Evan: Evan, CSM. we'll keep this fairly pragmatic.
[00:27] Jordan: Cool. objective for today: align on scope for the onboarding pilot, confirm network/security prerequisites, and land on who does what. especially want to understand latency targets — Priya you mentioned sub-200ms for short prompts?
[00:40] Priya: yeah so for the customer-facing chat flows we need p95 under 250ms ideally but realistic floor is 200ms for the smaller responses. for longer generative requests we'd accept higher, but startup UX needs that snappy thing.
[00:51] Maya: that's helpful. just to set expectations, for hosted we can get <200ms p95 for some of the smaller models, dedicated gives more consistent tail latencies. there's also batching tradeoffs.
[01:05] Liam: question on peering — we're primarily in GCP us-west1, and we need private peering to your control plane for telemetry. what does the CIDR look like, and do you require specific egress rules?
[01:16] Jordan: we'll send the peering CIDR list, there's also a lightweight NAT path for metrics. Maya, do you want to talk through the network doc?
[01:22] Maya: sure, i'll pull up the checklist. in staging we recommend a VPC peering for Private deployments, or if you prefer Dedicated via cloud marketplace we do managed VPC endpoints. our checklist includes: peering CIDRs, allow ports 443 and 8443, optional open for healthcheck IP ranges, and a short mtu note. also KMS integration — we support customer-managed keys in GCP KMS and AWS KMS, plus HSM if needed.
[01:46] Sofia: for KMS we need to know whether Redwood's control plane ever sees unencrypted tokens. is data encrypted end-to-end?
[01:53] Jordan: short answer, customer keys are used for at-rest encryption in Private, control plane does not have plaintext model data. i'll share the security brief but high level: TLS in transit, envelope encryption with customer KMS for Private deployments, and audit logs in both Dedicated and Private.
[02:09] Sofia: okay could you put the SOC2 report and the KMS integration writeup in a repo or link? we need to run it through our compliance treadmill.
[02:17] Evan: yes i'll attach the SOC2 and our KMS integration PDF after the call, plus the SAML SSO spec.
[02:24] Daniel: quick product question — for model pinning and rollout, can we do canary at traffic percent granularity? we want to gradually roll model updates without bringing down chat.
[02:33] Maya: yes, rollout policies support weighted traffic splits, canary by version, and automatic fallback to the previous model if error rate spikes. there is also per-route routing so you can route internal traffic to new model and external traffic to old.
[02:45] Priya: what about kv cache warmup? when we change models we see a cold-start cost. are there tools to warm the cache?
[02:53] Maya: we have cache priming APIs and a guidance runbook. you can pre-seed prefixes and we also support persistent KV cache across restarts in Dedicated. i'll include the runbook.
[03:05] Priya: perfect.
[03:08] Liam: network again — what latency should we expect for the control-plane calls during peering? any headroom estimates?
[03:14] Maya: in our staged benchmarks across us-west1 to our dedicated nodes you should see control-plane handshake add ~10–20ms, model inference depends on hardware. if you're on A100-class Dedicated you'll get lower per-token, but quantized models on T4s will be higher.
[03:30] Jordan: to help with economics we'll provide a sample cost calc for your prompt mix — that'll show how batching and kv cache affect unit cost.
[03:36] Priya: yes please, cost is a big driver for us. we ran some numbers in-house and OpenAI pricing would be cheaper per 1k tokens but we need determinism and SSO/audit.
[03:47] Jordan: totally — that’s where Dedicated/Private helps: predictable throughput and audit controls.
[03:52] Sofia: one security ask: can we restrict outgoing egress from Redwood runtime to only specific artifact stores? we need to make sure secrets don't leak.
[04:01] Maya: we support egress allowlists and network policies, also image scanning and ECR/GCR integration for custom containers. we'll put that in the security doc.
[04:11] Daniel: curious about monitoring — what dashboards do you provide for per-route latency and token cost?
[04:17] Evan: Redwood Console includes per-route latency p50/p95/p99, token breakdown, and alerting hooks. we can ship a dashboard template for your core chat endpoint.
[04:26] Priya: for the pilot we want to run a 7-day throughput test: 10k messages/day steady plus 3 burst windows. can you replicate bursts in staging?
[04:35] Maya: yes we can run a benchmark harness against staging and produce a CSV of latencies/throughput. we'll need your sample prompts and expected sequence lengths.
[04:43] Priya: i'll share a prompt set — it's messy, lots of code snippets and multi-turn context. expect larger token counts.
[04:50] Maya: that's important — multi-turn with KV cache benefits a lot from persistent cache. we'll include cache hit metrics in the report.
[04:58] Liam: one blocker in our infra: we have a central egress firewall that requires a ticket. what's the minimum set of IPs we need to whitelist?
[05:05] Jordan: we'll provide a condensed CIDR list. note there may be an occasional fallback IP for some control-plane features; we mark those optional.
[05:12] Sofia: on SSO, we use Okta. how's SAML integration? do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:18] Maya: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. single sign-on + RBAC mapping per team is supported, and you can map groups to roles.
[05:26] Priya: ok good.
[05:28] Evan: let's get explicit next steps — Jordan, you'll send network checklist and pricing. Maya you'll run the staging smoke test and share how caching looks. Priya/Liam you'll provide prompt set and open the firewall ticket. Sofia you'll review SOC2 and KMS docs.
[05:44] Priya: yep that's fine.
[05:46] Jordan: any concerns about timeline? we proposed a pilot starting next week and 7–14 days of benchmarking. is that realistic?
[05:55] Liam: depends on firewall ticket but we can aim to have peering approved in 3 business days. once that's in we can start.
[06:02] Sofia: compliance review will take longer but isn't necessarily a blocker for staging.
[06:08] Maya: action item: i'll spin up a staging endpoint and run a small synthetic test today to ensure connectivity; a 24-hour run for throughput we'll target and then the 7-day pilot once prompts are in.
[06:21] Jordan: perfect. any questions from the customer side?
[06:24] Daniel: one last thing — do you have a recommended quantization profile? we care about cost but not losing too much quality on our summarization flows.
[06:33] Maya: yes, we have quant profiles: 8-bit quant works for many retrieval and summarization tasks with small quality drop; for critical flows we recommend 16-bit or mixed precision. we'll include model/quant recs in the pilot doc.
[06:47] Priya: great.
[06:49] Evan: i'll summarize and email the notes + attach the docs.
[06:53] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links.

(Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and stutters; some product names transcribed differently, e.g., kv cache sometimes shows up as "KV cash" or "K V cache" in auto transcription.)
